title: Physics-Guided Learning of Meteorological Dynamics for Weather Downscaling and Forecasting

problem.claim: Traditional numerical weather prediction remains computationally intensive and physically incomplete, while deep learning models often ignore physical laws.

gap.claim: Existing deep learning weather models have limitations in interpretability and generalization because they often omit physical laws.

contributions.claim: PhyDL-NWP integrates physical equations and latent force parameterization into data-driven weather models.

The framework predicts weather variables from arbitrary spatiotemporal coordinates, computes physical terms through automatic differentiation, and uses a physics-informed loss aligned with governing dynamics.
The framework supports resolution-free downscaling through continuous-function weather modeling and fine-tunes pre-trained models with minimal overhead.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report up to 170× faster inference with only 55K parameters.
The authors report that experiments improve forecasting performance and physical consistency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Weather forecasting is important, but traditional numerical methods are computationally intensive and physically incomplete.
Deep learning can improve efficiency and accuracy but may neglect physical laws, limiting interpretability and generalization.
PhyDL-NWP integrates physical equations, latent force parameterization, automatic differentiation, and physics-informed loss into data-driven models.
The framework enables coordinate-based prediction, resolution-free downscaling, and lightweight fine-tuning of pre-trained models.
The authors report faster inference and improvements in forecasting performance and physical consistency.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines data-driven prediction with governing physical equations and a physics-informed loss.

interpretation.claim: Encoding domain constraints into model training may improve physical consistency while retaining deep learning efficiency.

application.claim: For scientific machine learning tasks, consider combining learned representations with differentiable domain constraints when physical consistency matters.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported weather forecasting and downscaling setting.
